title: EC2: instance families, sizes and what each one is for

videos.script: An instance type is the first thing you choose on EC2, and the easiest thing to choose badly. This lesson is about choosing it well. {{lab}} First, the lab. Nothing in this course touches a real AWS account. You talk to moto, an imitation of AWS that runs on your own computer. {{sheet}} And every price comes from AWS's public list, read by a short program you save once and keep. {{name}} Then the names. c7gd.xlarge looks like a stock code, and it is not one. It says five things about the machine, one letter at a time. {{families}} Over a thousand types are sorted into five categories. Each pairs processor and memory in its own ratio. You will work out what the wrong ratio costs in a month. {{sizes}} Sizes double, and so do their prices. So the size is a question about how you want to fail, not about money. Graviton is about a fifth cheaper, if your software runs on Arm. {{credits}} Last comes the burstable family. It sells you a share of the processor, and credits for the rest. For a machine that idles, it is a bargain. For one that does not, it is a trap, and you will see the arithmetic that tells them apart.
